props.description: Fired once with only the rows still accepted.

props.name: applyLabel
props.description: The button copy, given the live accepted count.

usageNotes: Proposals start accepted; a click withdraws one. The counts and the button derive from the toggles, never from the proposal.
Changed rows show both readings — was struck through, would-be beneath — so a change is never a mystery diff.
Applying seals the table; nothing can be applied twice.

items.title: Sieve Table
items.tagline: Surviving rows glide; hidden ones are counted.
items.description: A table sieved by status chips: pick a chip and the rows that survive glide to their new positions while the rest fold away — a layout move, never a reprint, because rows that teleport can't be followed and rows that reprint can't be trusted to be the same rows. Every chip carries its count, derived from the data, so the filter admits how much it hides.

props.name: statuses / rows
props.description: The chip set and the rows, each carrying a statusId.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column captions; the status column is added for you.

usageNotes: The chips are a real radiogroup; All is a first-class member, not an absence of filter.
Chip counts derive from the rows, so the filter admits what it hides.
Under reduced motion rows fade in place rather than travel.

items.title: Contact Ledger
items.tagline: The summary cannot disagree with the book.
items.description: A relationship grid that reads like a book: records grouped under alphabetical rails, each row carrying its tags, a pre-formatted last-touch date, and a three-bar strength meter labelled in words. The footer aggregates — count, linked share, average strength — are derived from the rows on render, so the summary cannot quietly disagree with the book it sums.

props.name: records
props.description: Name, place, tags, pre-formatted last touch, strength 0–3, optional link.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: Tags shown per row before the +N overflow.

usageNotes: For working ten thousand rows, reach for the ledger — this one is for reading a hundred relationships honestly.
Strength pairs bars with words; the meter is never colour alone.
Dates are pre-formatted strings, so the grid never reads a clock and cannot drift from the server.

items.title: Switchyard
items.tagline: A rule, read at rest.
items.description: A workflow drawn as cards on a dotted yard: a trigger, then the switches — each condition a clause of words and chips, entities and values set apart from the prose so the rule reads as a rule. The cards hang off one drawn spine, arriving down it in order. This is the still, legible cousin of the flow instruments: nothing here simulates — it states, because a rule you are about to enable deserves to be read at rest.

props.name: nodes
props.description: Trigger and condition cards; conditions carry clauses of words and chips.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the drawn canvas.

usageNotes: Chips separate entities from values from prose — a rule whose parts all look alike cannot be audited by eye.
Quantity flow belongs to flow-diagram; this instrument states logic, it never simulates it.
The spine draws once on entry; under reduced motion it is simply there.

items.title: Insight Reel
items.tagline: The claim, with its evidence scrubable.
items.description: Findings on a reel: one insight at a time — the claim as a sentence with its subject chipped, the deltas beside it pre-formatted and toned, and the series behind the claim drawn on the spark instrument so the reader can scrub the evidence themselves. Dots page the reel; each card offers one follow-up, because an insight worth surfacing is worth asking about.

props.name: insights
props.description: Lead, subject chip, leadAfter, toned deltas, a series, one follow-up.

props.name: onFollowUp
props.description: Fired when a card's offered ask is taken.

usageNotes: Deltas are pre-formatted strings — the reel formats nothing, so it can never round a claim differently than the system that made it.
The chart is spark-chart, crosshair and all; the reel adds paging, never chart mechanics.
One follow-up per card. A finding with five suggested asks is a menu, not an insight.

items.title: Trim Panel
items.tagline: Adjustments narrated, never silent.
items.description: The inspector with an agent's hands on it: width, height, radius, and opacity read out as rolling numerals while the stage element re-trims live on the glide spring — every adjustment narrated, because a tool that changes your design silently is indistinguishable from a bug. The fields are the record, the stage is the proof, and the two cannot disagree: both read from the same values.

props.name: initial / steps
props.description: The starting reading and the narrated adjustments, one per interval.

props.name: interval
props.description: Seconds between adjustments; the walk is mount-driven, never the wall clock.

usageNotes: Stage and fields read from the same values, so the preview cannot disagree with the record.
Each step carries its narration; the note line is a polite live region.
Under reduced motion the stage re-trims without travel but the numerals still roll — a changing number is information.

items.title: Blue Pencil
items.tagline: The verbs hand the text back out.
items.description: The editor's blue pencil: select a passage and a small toolbar of rewrite verbs springs up anchored to the selection — explain, improve, shorten, tone. The verbs hand the selected text back out; the pencil never rewrites anything itself, because the surface that edits and the model that edits must be separable for either to be trusted.

props.name: children
props.description: The passage the pencil works over.

props.name: verbs / onVerb
props.description: The rewrite verbs, and the hand-off carrying the selected text.

usageNotes: The pencil never rewrites — it hands the selection out, so the surface and the model stay separable.
Anchored from the selection's own rectangle and clamped to the passage box, so it cannot escape its stage.
Collapsing the selection withdraws the toolbar; selectionchange catches keyboard, double-click, and drag alike.

items.title: Workbench Rail
items.tagline: One light that travels, not many that blink.
items.description: The workspace rail: primary destinations, then the running conversations, with one gliding highlight that travels to whatever the pointer is over — a single shared element, so the hover reads as one light moving rather than many lighting up. The invite quota is a printed fraction, not a paywall surprise, and the whole rail folds to a spine when the work needs the width back.

props.name: primary / threads
props.description: Destinations, then the running conversations under their own heading.

props.name: activeId / onSelect
props.description: Controlled selection; uncontrolled falls back to the first destination.

props.name: quota
props.description: The printed seat fraction — used, limit, and what it counts.

props.name: defaultCollapsed
props.description: Start folded to the spine.

usageNotes: The travelling highlight is one shared layout element on the snap spring — hover reads as a light moving, and it is hover only; selection is carried by state and aria-current.
Print the quota before anyone hits it; a seat limit discovered at the eleventh invite is a paywall surprise.
Collapsed is a real state with its own affordance, not a squashed layout.

items.title: App Window Vignette
items.tagline: Software working, without a screenshot.
items.description: A product window that paints itself in: the chrome lands first, sidebar rows cascade, the spark line draws its series, and the headline number rolls up on the readout — the standard product-demo vignette for a hero that wants to show software working without shipping a screenshot. Purely presentational: the scene reads to assistive tech as one image with an honest label.

props.name: rows
props.description: Sidebar rows that cascade in; the first reads active.

props.name: metric
props.description: The headline number the readout rolls to.

props.name: series / seriesLabel
props.description: The line the spark instrument draws.

usageNotes: Purely presentational — every interactive-looking part is decoration at this scale, marked aria-hidden behind one label.
Seat it in a hero's vignette slot; hero-split-ledger shows the seating.
The chart and numeral are the real instruments (spark-chart, readout), so the vignette inherits their reduced-motion behaviour.

items.title: Handset Vignette
items.tagline: The phone view, without a video file.
items.description: A handset with an app scene scrolling on a slow loop — the mobile-demo vignette for a hero that wants to show the phone view without a video file. The card list is doubled and translated by half, so the loop never jumps; hovering rests the scroll, because a reader leaning in deserves a still page.

props.name: cards
props.description: The scene's cards, looped seamlessly.

props.name: loopSeconds
props.description: One full scroll cycle.

usageNotes: The loop is a doubled list translated by half — it cannot jump, whatever the card count.
Hover rests the scroll; motion that ignores an attentive reader is motion working against the page.
Reduced motion holds the scene still at the top of the list.

items.title: Exchange Vignette
items.tagline: A conversation's shape, on a loop.
items.description: A chat moment that loops politely: bubbles land one beat at a time, the finished exchange rests long enough to be read whole, then it clears and begins again. A vignette, not a chat — the beats are fixed, nothing is interactive, and the scene reads to assistive tech as one image with the transcript as its label. The working thread is volley-thread.

props.name: beats
props.description: Fixed ask/answer beats, landed in order.

props.name: holdSeconds / restSeconds
props.description: Beat spacing, and how long the finished exchange rests.

usageNotes: The rest matters: a loop that clears the moment it finishes is a loop nobody has read.
Fixed beats by design — a vignette that accepts input is a broken chat, not a scene.
Reduced motion prints the whole exchange at rest.

items.title: Voice Note Vignette
items.tagline: The shape of a voice.
items.description: A voice note as a scene: speaker, a fixed waveform, and a play head that sweeps the bars — each brightening as the head passes, the way a message app renders playback. The waveform is provided data, not audio analysis, and nothing plays; it is the shape of a voice for heroes about talking to software.

props.name: waveform
props.description: Bar heights 0–1 — a fixed shape, so SSR and client agree.

props.name: speaker / duration
props.description: Who left it and its pre-formatted length.

props.name: sweepSeconds
props.description: One playback sweep.

usageNotes: Nothing plays — the vignette is playback's look, not an audio element.
The waveform is data, so the same note renders identically on server and client.
Reduced motion rests the head a third of the way in, bars behind it lit.

items.title: Search Lens Vignette
items.tagline: Finding, staged.
items.description: A search moment: the field focuses, the query types itself, three results settle in, the scene rests, then it clears and runs again. A vignette of finding — fixed beats, nothing interactive, one image to assistive tech — for heroes about products where the answer is a search away. The working palette is command-deck; this is its portrait.

props.name: query / results
props.description: What types itself, and the three that settle.

props.name: restSeconds
props.description: How long the settled scene holds before looping.

usageNotes: command-deck is the working instrument; this portrait must never grow keyboard handling.
Type speed is fixed and mount-driven, so the scene is deterministic under SSR.
Reduced motion prints the settled scene and stays.

items.title: Hub Vignette
items.tagline: The product in the middle of everything.
items.description: A centre node with its services arranged on a ring, links drawn from each to the core and a pulse travelling every line in turn — the integration scene, for heroes about products that sit in the middle of other tools. Positions are computed from index and count, so the layout is identical on server and client, and the pulse order is fixed.

props.name: core / nodes
props.description: The centre and the ring of services.

props.name: radius
props.description: Ring radius in pixels.

usageNotes: Positions derive from index and count — no measurement, no randomness, identical SSR.
One pulse at a time, in roster order; six pulses at once is traffic, not a story.
Reduced motion draws every link complete and rests a lit dot at each node.

items.title: File Run Vignette
items.tagline: Ingestion with an honest tally.
items.description: Files flowing a drawn path into a destination, one departing at a time, with the landed tally rolling on the readout — the ingestion scene, for heroes about pipelines and imports. Departures are a mount-driven cycle and the tally counts landings honestly: it only rolls when a chip arrives.

props.name: files / destination
props.description: What departs, and where it lands.

props.name: cadence
props.description: Seconds between departures.

usageNotes: The tally is a readout fed by landings — it can never run ahead of the chips.
The rails are fixed curves; nothing about the path is measured at runtime.
Reduced motion rests the chips and reads the tally complete.

items.title: Wave Meter Vignette
items.tagline: A signal that reads live, honestly.
items.description: A metering loop: bars breathe through a fixed pattern that rotates, with one peak marked and named — the live-signal scene, for heroes about telemetry and throughput. The pattern is data, the rotation is a mount-driven cycle, and nothing is random, so server and client always paint the same meter.

props.name: pattern / peakIndex
props.description: Fixed heights 0–1 and which one is the marked peak.

props.name: cycleSeconds
props.description: One full pattern rotation.

usageNotes: The pattern is provided data — a meter that invents its signal at render breaks SSR determinism.
The peak is marked and captioned; an unexplained tallest bar is decoration.
Reduced motion holds the pattern still with the peak lit.

items.title: Iso Stack Vignette
items.tagline: The system, in layers.
items.description: An isometric stack rising into place, each layer labelled on its edge — the architecture scene, for heroes that want layers of a system without a diagramming tool. Plates are CSS-transformed divs, so they theme like everything else and cost nothing to load.

props.name: layers
props.description: Bottom-up; the top plate carries the accent.

usageNotes: Pure CSS transforms — no canvas, no 3D library, themes for free.
Label layers bottom-up the way the reader stacks them mentally.
Reduced motion stands the stack assembled.

items.title: Iso Floor Vignette
items.tagline: A route, tile by tile.
items.description: An isometric tile floor with a route pulsing across it, one tile at a time — the infrastructure scene, for heroes about things moving through a system. The floor is a CSS-rotated grid, the route is fixed data, and the pulse is a mount-driven cycle: deterministic everywhere.

props.name: size / route
props.description: Tiles per side, and the row-major route that lights.

props.name: cadence
props.description: Seconds between pulses.

usageNotes: The route is authored, not pathfound — a vignette should never surprise its own page.
The loop clears and re-runs with a short rest, so the route reads as a journey, not a flicker.
Reduced motion holds the whole route lit.

items.title: Hover Swap
items.tagline: Two readings, one label.
items.description: A label with two readings: at rest it says one thing, and under hover or focus it rolls to the alternate — the old line leaving as the new one arrives, both clipped to the label's own box. For links whose hover state has something to add, nav items, and buttons with a second thought. Both readings live in the accessible name, so the roll is presentation and never information.

props.name: children / alternate
props.description: The resting reading and the one it rolls to.

props.name: direction
props.description: Roll direction.

usageNotes: Both readings reserve the wider box, so the label never resizes mid-roll.
The accessible name carries both readings, always — the roll is never the only source.
Focus triggers the roll too; keyboard users get the second thought.

items.title: Relay Tip
items.tagline: One label travelling, not four blinking.
items.description: One tip surface, relayed: instead of each trigger owning a tooltip that pops and dies, a single shared surface glides from trigger to trigger, morphing to fit each caption — so moving along a row of controls reads as one label travelling, not four labels blinking. Each trigger keeps a per-trigger description for assistive tech; the relay is presentation, the semantics stay stationary.

props.name: stops
props.description: Triggers and what the tip says over each.

props.name: offset
props.description: Gap between trigger and tip.

usageNotes: The travel is a shared layout element on the snap spring; entering from nothing still pops, and leaving the last trigger withdraws it.
Every trigger keeps its own role=tooltip description — screen readers never depend on the travelling surface.
Reduced motion shows the tip over each trigger without travel.

items.title: Folio Table
items.tagline: Leaf through it; pour it into the ledger.
items.description: The paged edition of the working grid: a folio turns pages instead of scrolling ten thousand rows, columns can be re-picked from a rail of chips, and the page turn is a directional slide so going back reads as going back. Paging belongs to pagination-rail — this table seats it. For the virtualized firehose, the ledger remains the instrument; a folio is for datasets you leaf through, not pour.

props.name: columns / rows
props.description: Columns (re-pickable) and pre-formatted row cells by column id.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page; the page count derives.

usageNotes: Paging is pagination-rail's — keyboard, previews, and clamping come with it.
The last visible column cannot be hidden; a table with zero columns is a bug shipped as a feature.
Page turns slide from the direction of travel, so back reads as back.

items.title: Stage Rail Vignette
items.tagline: The pipeline, one light at a time.
items.description: A pipeline as a scene, in either orientation: a row of icon tiles with one light roving along them and a caption naming whoever holds it, or a column rolling the stages through a lit focus band — each stage sliding to its next seat, so the edges wrap instead of jumping. For feature cards about systems that do things in order.

props.name: orient
props.description: Tiles with a roving light and caption, or rows rolling through a focus band.

props.name: stages / holdSeconds
props.description: The stages, and how long each holds the light.

usageNotes: The column wraps circularly — each row springs to its next seat rather than the list scrolling past a window.
Hover rests the march; a reader leaning in deserves a still page.
Reduced motion stops on the middle stage with every label legible.

items.title: Icon Reel Vignette
items.tagline: Everything it touches, drifting past.
items.description: A reel of icon tiles drifting past behind edge fades — the everything-it-touches scene at card scale, where the marquee hall is a whole section. The track is doubled and translated by half so the loop never jumps, and hovering rests the reel. Purely presentational, marked as one image.

props.name: icons
props.description: The tiles — each names what it stands for, for screen readers.

props.name: reelSeconds
props.description: Seconds for one full pass.

usageNotes: Card-scale by design — for a full-width band of logos, reach for the marquee hall section instead.
The doubled track makes the loop seamless; never halve the list to save renders.
Reduced motion holds the reel still from its start.

items.title: Arc Gallery Vignette
items.tagline: A fan of cards, taking turns.
items.description: Cards fanned along an arc, each taking a turn at the front: every advance sends the whole fan one seat around, so a card leaves the lead by swinging to the wing rather than vanishing. The washes are gradients, not images — the scene stays theme-aware and weightless. For heroes about places, projects, or portfolios.

props.name: arc
props.description: Bow the fan upward, or hang it downward.

props.name: cards / holdSeconds
props.description: The fan, and how long each card leads.

usageNotes: Positions are circular offsets from the lead — computed, deterministic, identical SSR.
Washes are gradient pairs, so the cards recolour with the theme instead of shipping images.
Hover rests the turn; reduced motion holds the fan with the first card leading.

items.title: Copresence Vignette
items.tagline: Two hands, one surface, no claim.
items.description: Two hands on the same surface: named cursors gliding their own errands, a live selection with its measurements printed — or a work card walked between columns — and a remark that arrives, holds, and clears. Everything runs on one shared clock of authored keyframes, so the loop reads as a morning's minute, not a screensaver. The multiplayer moment as a scene rather than a claim.

props.name: scene
props.description: A headline under live selection, or a card being walked between columns.

props.name: hands / remark
props.description: Who is here, and the comment one of them leaves.

props.name: loopSeconds
props.description: One full loop of the shared clock.

usageNotes: All movement is authored keyframes on one clock — cursors, card, and remark stay in step at any loop length.
Tones come in as CSS colors, so the cast recolours per deployment without touching the scene.
Reduced motion parks the hands mid-errand and keeps the remark shown.

items.title: Distill Vignette
items.tagline: A mess on both sides, a plan in the middle.
items.description: Many inputs, one product: two columns of sources fold into the centre one by one — each chip lights, leans toward the middle, and dims as spent — and when the last is in, the product stamps itself finished. The scene is the argument for anything that reads a mess and returns a plan.

props.name: left / right
props.description: The raw material, one column per side.

props.name: product / stamped
props.description: What it becomes, and the line stamped when finished.

props.name: stepSeconds / restSeconds
props.description: Seconds between folds, and the hold before the loop resets.

usageNotes: Sources fold alternating left and right so the columns drain evenly — the order is fixed, never random.
The centre counts folds honestly and only stamps when every source is in.
Reduced motion shows the finished state: everything folded, the stamp standing.

items.title: Bubble Pop
items.tagline: The sheet everyone fights over, shipped.
items.description: A sheet of bubble wrap you actually get to pop: every bubble is a real button, each press squashes it flat with a crisp snap and a four-fleck puff, and the counter underneath keeps honest score. Pop them all and the sheet takes a breath, then re-inflates in a cascade — because the only thing better than bubble wrap is more bubble wrap.

props.name: columns / rows
props.description: The sheet's dimensions.

props.name: onAllPopped
props.description: Fires when the last bubble goes.

usageNotes: Every bubble is a focusable button with its own label — the toy is fully keyboard-playable.
Puff angles come from a fixed table; two visitors popping the same bubble see the same puff.
Reduced motion swaps pops instantly — flat is flat, no squash, no puff.

items.title: Poke Pudding
items.tagline: It jiggles. It judges. It forgives.
items.description: A pudding with a face and opinions about being poked. Press and it squashes; release and it jiggles back on a real spring; poke it three times fast and it goes briefly dizzy before composing itself. Not a physics simulation — a character, which is why the eyes matter more than the wobble.

props.name: flavor
props.description: The top layer's tint.

props.name: onPoke
props.description: Fires per poke with the running count.

usageNotes: Rapid pokes re-squash from wherever the jiggle currently is — the spring is interruptible by design.
The blink runs on a fixed interval; the dizzy face needs three pokes inside a second and a half.
Reduced motion swaps between two still poses and keeps the face.

items.title: Stamp Pad
items.tagline: Approval, applied liberally.
items.description: A blank sheet and a tray of stamps: click anywhere and the next stamp slams down at that exact spot — oversized, slightly rotated, thunking to rest with an impact ring. Rotations and colors cycle from fixed tables, the sheet holds two dozen before it clears itself, and keyboard users stamp a tidy grid of their own.

props.name: stamps
props.description: The rotation of stamps; defaults to six joyful glyphs.

props.name: cap
props.description: Stamps held before the sheet clears itself.

usageNotes: Stamp order, rotation, and color all cycle from fixed arrays — no randomness, identical replay.
Clear fades the sheet with a cascade stagger; the cap clear happens before the next stamp lands.
Reduced motion places stamps at rest instantly, no ring, instant clear.

items.title: Cookie Bite
items.tagline: Five bites, no regrets, free refills.
items.description: A cookie you eat one click at a time: five bites disappear from the rim in a fixed order through an SVG mask, each with a startle squash and three crumbs arcing to the plate. When it is gone, the plate admits “worth it” — and a fresh one springs in, because grief should be brief.

props.name: bites
props.description: How many bites the cookie survives (3–6).

props.name: onBite / onFinish
props.description: Per bite, and when only crumbs remain.

usageNotes: Bite positions are a precomputed table — the same cookie every time, which is how cookies should work.
A polite live region counts the bites for screen readers.
Reduced motion swaps the mask instantly — no crumbs, no squash, instant refill.

items.title: Hatchling
items.tagline: Three taps. One wink. No omelette.
items.description: An egg that hatches in three taps: the first jolts a crack into it, the second chips the shell, and the third pops the top so a chick can rise, look both ways, and wink. A fourth tap tucks everything back in for the next visitor. The caption underplays the whole thing, which is the correct amount of ceremony.

props.name: onHatch
props.description: Fires when the chick appears.

usageNotes: Cracks draw in with pathLength tweens; the shell pop is the only spring with real theatre.
The look-left-look-right-wink is authored keyframes on one clock — the same performance every hatch.
Reduced motion steps through four still states: whole, cracked, chipped, hatched.

items.title: Yo-yo Drop
items.tagline: Hold to sleep. Release to come home.
items.description: A yo-yo that sleeps while you hold and rewinds when you let go: press and the disc drops the string's length and spins in place, string faintly humming; release and it climbs home on a crisp spring with one small settle bounce. Hold too long and it wobbles — it has somewhere to be. The caption keeps score in three words or fewer.

props.name: stringLength
props.description: How far it drops, in pixels.

props.name: onReturn
props.description: Fires on a clean rewind.

usageNotes: Space and Enter hold it down too — the toy is fully keyboard-playable.
The sleep spin is a linear tween on the painted edge stripe; the rewind is the only theatrical spring.
Reduced motion swaps between parked and dropped instantly, no spin.

items.title: Soap Bubble
items.tagline: Hold to blow. Let go to let go.
items.description: A wand you blow through by holding: the film grows from the ring with an iridescent sheen and a nervous wobble, and on release the bubble detaches, drifts up a gentle S, and pops into droplets at the top of its rise. Release too early and it just wisps out — bubbles have standards. Two in flight at most; patience is part of the toy.

props.name: onPop
props.description: Fires when a bubble completes its rise.

usageNotes: The flight path is authored keyframes — every bubble takes the same S, which is somehow funnier.
The sheen is two gradient layers color-mixed from tokens, so it recolours with the theme.
Reduced motion shows the film at a fixed size and lets released bubbles fade in place.

items.title: Applause Hold
items.tagline: Hold for the ovation you meant.
items.description: Press-and-hold applause that builds: the hands clap faster the longer you hold, the meter fills, and at four seconds it tips into a standing ovation — glow, flecks, the works. Release and the ovation drains politely. Where the heart tap is a single thank-you, this is the whole room getting to its feet.

props.name: ovationAfter
props.description: Seconds of hold before the room stands.

props.name: onOvation
props.description: Fires when the ovation lands.

usageNotes: Clap tempo steps through a fixed table — the crescendo is authored, not random.
All timers are cleaned up on release and unmount; rapid re-holds resume from the drained meter.
Reduced motion swaps the clapping for a stepped meter and a mono clap count.

items.title: Tea Dunk
items.tagline: Steeped, with enthusiasm bonuses.
items.description: A mug and a teabag on a string: drag it under and ripples ring the entry, lift it out and it drips, and the water deepens toward amber as it steeps. Park it and wait, or dunk like you mean it — full dunks steep faster, which is the toy quietly rewarding enthusiasm. At full steep the surface steams and the caption declares it done.

props.name: steepRate
props.description: Steep per second while submerged.

props.name: onReady
props.description: Fires when the tea is done.

usageNotes: Arrow keys dunk in steps — the drag is never the only way in.
Water colour interpolates by color-mix percentage, so the amber tracks the theme's warmth token.
Reduced motion keeps 1:1 dragging but stills the ripples, drips, and steam.

items.title: Balloon Pump
items.tagline: Six stages. You know how this ends.
items.description: A hand pump, a balloon, and the outcome everyone is waiting for: each press drives the plunger, sends a puff down the hose, and stretches the balloon one stage larger — trembling faintly at stage five, gone at six in a fling of rubber scraps. A beat later the next colour is on the nozzle, deflated and optimistic. The pop is anticipated, earned, and immediately forgiven.

props.name: stages
props.description: Pumps the balloon survives (4–8).

props.name: onPop
props.description: Fires with the departed balloon's colour.

usageNotes: Balloon colours cycle a fixed token palette; scrap vectors are a fixed table.
The stage-five tremble is the anticipation — do not remove it, it is most of the joke.
Reduced motion swaps sizes instantly and skips scraps; the caption still says POP.

items.title: Top Spin
items.tagline: Spin, wobble, fall, forgive.
items.description: A spinning top with honest physics feel: flick it and it spins with your velocity, coasts down on fixed friction, enters the death wobble every top owes its audience, and tips over with one rock. Click a fallen top and it stands back up, ready to go again. The caption narrates in four states and never oversells.

props.name: onFall
props.description: Fires when the wobble wins.

usageNotes: The flick reads real pointer velocity, clamped into an authored range — physical feel, deterministic bounds.
A plain click or Enter gives the standard spin, so the toy needs no drag to enjoy.
Reduced motion steps through standing, spinning, and fallen stills.

items.title: Clack Beads
items.tagline: Momentum, conserved theatrically.
items.description: Five beads on a rod: flick the free one into the cluster and the impact travels — the struck bead compresses, a clack tick flashes at contact, and the far bead shoots out, coasts, and wanders lazily back. Not a physics engine; an authored choreography tuned until it feels like one, which is cheaper and never misses. The pendulum cousin lives elsewhere — these slide.

props.name: beads
props.description: Beads on the rod (3–7).

props.name: onClack
props.description: Fires at contact.

usageNotes: The transfer is one authored sequence — flick, travel, squash, eject, wander home — identical every time.
Mid-sequence flicks restart from current positions rather than queueing; the toy always answers the hand.
Reduced motion swaps positions instantly and keeps the clack caption.

items.title: Pinwheel Breeze
items.tagline: Your cursor is the weather.
items.description: A paper pinwheel that spins from the breeze your cursor makes: pointer speed becomes angular velocity, friction takes it back, and at rest it sways like something waiting outside a shop. Fast enough and the vanes blend into a blur disc. A click gives it a push, so the breeze is never the only way to play.

props.name: onSpin
props.description: Fires when a push takes it past brisk.

usageNotes: Velocity is clamped, friction is fixed — the weather is yours but the physics are the house's.
The blur disc is layered opacity, not a filter, so it stays cheap.
Reduced motion steps the wheel a quarter turn per click, no coasting.

items.title: Kite Tug
items.tagline: One tug. One loop. Wheee.
items.description: A diamond kite bobbing on a sagging line — tug it and the line snaps taut, the kite dives, swoops a loop with its tail streaming, and settles back into the idle sky. The line is one quadratic path whose sag breathes with the kite; the rope simulation lives elsewhere in the catalog, and this scene does not need it. The caption says “wheee” exactly once per swoop.

props.name: onSwoop
props.description: Fires as the loop begins.

usageNotes: The swoop is authored keyframes with the nose leading via synced rotate times — the same aerobatics every tug.
Double tugs during a swoop are ignored; the kite finishes its sentence.
Reduced motion holds a fixed pose and swaps briefly to a swooped still.

items.title: Paper Plane
items.tagline: Fold. Aim. Launch. Stick it.
items.description: A folded dart that launches from its pad, climbs, banks, dips, loops once, and glides home to stick the landing — with a dashed trail drawing in behind it and fading after touchdown. The whole lap is one authored flight; a second loop is a prop away. For empty states, sent-confirmations, and anyone who misses classrooms.

props.name: loops
props.description: Mid-air loops per lap.

props.name: onLand
props.description: Fires at touchdown.

usageNotes: Rotation keyframes share the flight's times so the nose always leads — the banking is the craft.
The trail is the flight path itself, dash-drawn behind the plane and faded after landing.
Reduced motion steps pad, apex, and pad stills with the trail shown static.

items.title: Crank Tune
items.tagline: Every quarter turn earns a note.
items.description: A music box you crank by hand: drag the knob in circles and the arm tracks your pointer exactly, emitting a note glyph every quarter turn that floats up and away. Crank backwards and it plays nothing — the box is honest about which direction music comes from. Enter turns it a quarter turn for anyone playing by keyboard.

props.name: onNote
props.description: Fires per note, with its position in the cycle.

usageNotes: The crank is 1:1 direct manipulation — angle unwrapping accumulates full turns rather than snapping at the seam.
Notes only emit on forward cranking; reversing moves the arm and plays nothing.
Reduced motion keeps the 1:1 crank and lands notes at their end position without the float.

items.title: Gumball Run
items.tagline: Turn the knob, watch it ride.
items.description: A gumball machine that actually delivers: turn the knob and a ball leaves the globe, rides the chute on an authored path, and bounces into the tray where the count ticks up. Colours cycle in fixed order, the globe visibly empties, and when it runs dry it restocks in a cascade. Three balls may be in transit before the machine asks you to wait.

props.name: capacity
props.description: Gumballs served before the globe restocks.

props.name: onServe
props.description: Fires with each served colour.

usageNotes: The chute travel is an authored keyframe path matching the drawn SVG — the ball never leaves its pipe.
The globe's cluster is a fixed table that empties as balls are served, so the machine cannot lie about its stock.
Reduced motion drops the ball straight into the tray and restocks at once.

items.title: Toast Pop
items.tagline: The shudder before the leap.
items.description: A toaster that makes you wait for it: push the lever, the bread sinks, the slot glows, the crust browns, and just before the end the whole machine gives one small shudder of anticipation. Then it leaps, lands askew, sheds crumbs, and takes a topping stamp. The suspense is the feature — a toaster that popped instantly would be a notification, and the catalog has those.

props.name: toastSeconds
props.description: How long the wait lasts (1–6).

props.name: onPop
props.description: Fires with the topping that lands.

usageNotes: Browning is a color-mix ramp over the toasting duration — the bread is never a sprite swap.
Toppings cycle a fixed set; the stamp thunks down on `flick` after the leap settles.
Reduced motion skips the glow ramp, shudder, and leap; the toast simply arrives topped.

items.title: Pull Cord
items.tagline: Past the threshold, let there be light.
items.description: A pendant lamp with a cord you actually pull: drag the bead down and the cord stretches under your hand, release past the threshold and the room floods warm — the cord snapping back into a couple of swings while dust motes drift up through the light. Let go short of the threshold and nothing happens, which is exactly what a real cord does.

props.name: defaultOn
props.description: Whether the room starts lit.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Fires with the new state.

usageNotes: The near-miss is deliberate — a short pull snaps back without toggling, which is most of the tactility.
The cord swing is a multi-keyframe tween, not a spring, because a spring cannot hold three positions.
Reduced motion keeps 1:1 dragging, swaps the light instantly, and omits the motes.

items.title: Domino Run
items.tagline: One push, nine falls, one flag.
items.description: A row of dominoes and one honest click: the first tile goes over, the topple propagates down the line on a cascade stagger with a dust puff at each base, and the last one raises a little flag. A beat later they all stand back up in reverse, ready to go again. The whole run is index math — no physics, no randomness, and it never fails to finish.

props.name: tiles
props.description: Tiles in the run (5–14).

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Fires when the flag goes up.

usageNotes: Fall delays come from cascade(count), so longer runs tighten their stagger instead of dragging.
Tiles pivot on their bottom edge — the transform-origin is the whole illusion.
Reduced motion swaps the whole row to fallen at once, raises the flag, and stands them back up after the beat.

items.title: Googly Eyes
items.tagline: They are watching. Politely.
items.description: A pair of stick-on plastic eyes that follow your cursor with a slight spring lag, blink on their own schedule (every third one a double), and go cross-eyed when you get too close to the bridge of their nose. Boop them and the pupils rattle loose before settling back to work. Nothing here re-renders — tracking rides motion values from a document listener.

props.name: size
props.description: Eye diameter in pixels; everything scales off it.

props.name: onBoop
props.description: Fires on each boop.

usageNotes: Pupil offsets are clamped inside each socket, so the eyes never look like they escaped.
The jiggle rides on top of live tracking as a summed overlay — a boop never pauses the watching.
Reduced motion keeps the tracking (it is the point) but drops the lag, blinking, and jiggle.

items.title: Duckling Trail
items.tagline: A conga line with feathers.
items.description: A pond where a mother duck follows your pointer and her ducklings conga behind her, each one springing off the last so the line bunches at rest and stretches when she moves. Leave the pond and the family drifts to the bank to wait. Arrow keys and Enter walk her between waypoints, because the toy should not need a mouse.

props.name: ducklings
props.description: How many follow (1–5).

usageNotes: The chain is springs of springs — no animation loop, and the lag is the physics.
Hook count is fixed at the maximum and sliced by the prop, so changing the family size never breaks the rules of hooks.
Reduced motion snaps the family to fixed offsets with no bobbing or ripples.

items.title: Tail Wag
items.tagline: Wag rate is a function of distance.
items.description: A dog behind a button whose tail wags faster the closer your cursor gets — a lazy sway across the room, a blur of enthusiasm up close. Press the button and the whole body joins in: rump shimmy, ears up, one heart. The caption escalates from “good dog” to “GOOD DOG”, which is the entire joke and it lands every time.

props.name: onPet
props.description: Fires when the button is pressed.

usageNotes: Distance maps to four rate buckets, and only a bucket change restarts the tween — never the pointer move itself.
The tail pivots at its base; it is an HTML element, so transform-origin behaves normally.
Reduced motion swaps four fixed tail angles by bucket, with no loop.

items.title: Critter Choir
items.tagline: Four voices, one accidental chord.
items.description: Four round critters in a row, each with its own pitch: tap one and it inflates, opens its mouth, and sends a note glyph rising — higher and lighter as you move up the scale. Tap all four inside a second and a half and they harmonize, notes fanning out over a glow. At rest they breathe slightly out of sync, which is most of the charm.

props.name: onChord
props.description: Fires when all four sing inside the window.

usageNotes: Pitch reads visually: higher critters rise their notes further and inflate less, so the row scans as a scale.
The chord window is a rolling ledger of tap timestamps kept in a ref — checked in the handler, never in render.
Reduced motion holds an inflated still with the note shown, and the chord glow appears as a state.

items.title: Little Door
items.tagline: Knock three times. Regret it.
items.description: A tiny door in the baseboard and whoever lives behind it. Two knocks rattle the frame and move the caption along; the third cracks it open on its hinge, a pair of eyes blinks out, and a beat later it slams — shaking dust from the frame and leaving one word of review. Swap the resident for a flower if you would rather be greeted than judged.

props.name: resident
props.description: Who answers on the third knock.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires when the door cracks open.

usageNotes: The door opens by scaling from its hinge edge rather than rotating in 3D — no perspective, no Safari surprises.
The whole bit resets itself after the slam, so the toy is always ready to be rude again.
Reduced motion swaps closed and open stills with the resident shown, and skips the dust.

items.title: Piñata Tap
items.tagline: Five swings, then candy everywhere.
items.description: A piñata on a rope that takes five swings: each hit sends it swinging harder, tears another fringe strip loose, and moves the caption one word closer to inevitable. The fifth splits it open and a dozen candies arc out on authored gravity to land scattered on the floor. A beat later a fresh one drops in, because the only correct number of piñatas is another one.

props.name: hits
props.description: Swings it survives (3–7).

props.name: onBurst
props.description: Fires when it finally goes.

usageNotes: Damage is cumulative and visible — fringe tears in fixed order, so the state is always readable.
Candy vectors are a fixed table arcing under an authored gravity curve; the same party every time.
Reduced motion swaps damage stills and shows the candy already landed.

items.title: Gift Unwrap
items.tagline: Ribbon first. Always ribbon first.
items.description: A wrapped present that opens in two beats: the first click pulls the ribbon loose and slides the bands off, the second pops the lid tumbling away as the gift rises on a glow. A third re-wraps it with the next gift queued. Making the ribbon its own beat is the whole trick — unwrapping in one click is a reveal, unwrapping in two is a gift.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires with the revealed gift.

usageNotes: Gifts cycle a fixed set of three, each with its own dry caption — no randomness, so a demo replays identically.
Clicks during a transition are ignored; the box always finishes its sentence.
Reduced motion steps the four stills: wrapped, unwrapped, open, wrapped again.

items.title: Medal Swing
items.tagline: It lands, it swings, it shines.
items.description: A medal that drops in on its lanyard, swings itself to rest on a decaying tween, and then keeps catching the light on a slow glint cycle. Hover for an extra flash; click because nobody can leave a hanging medal alone. Three tiers, each tinted from the palette rather than painted gold, so it belongs to whatever theme it lands in.

props.name: tier
props.description: Which metal, tinted from tokens.

props.name: label
props.description: The caption's right half.

usageNotes: The settle is a decaying keyframe tween, never a spring — a spring cannot hold four diminishing swings.
The glint re-triggers on hover only when one is not already running, so hover-spam cannot stack sheens.
Reduced motion presents the medal already hung, with a single static highlight on click.

items.title: High Five
items.tagline: Leave one hanging. See what happens.
items.description: An open palm waiting to be met: click and a second hand swings in, the two connect with a shockwave ring and a scatter of impact flecks, then part again. Double-tap too fast and the incoming hand whiffs straight past — the caption calls it, which is funnier than landing it. At rest the palm just breathes and invites.

props.name: onFive
props.description: Fires on a connected five, not on a whiff.

usageNotes: The whiff is a separate authored path, not a failed version of the hit — the miss has to look intentional.
Timing comes from event timestamps in handlers; nothing reads the clock during render.
Reduced motion swaps a met still (or a missed one) for a beat with the ring shown static.

items.title: Level Chime
items.tagline: The bar fills, the number carries.
items.description: An experience bar that levels up properly: each tap adds XP with a floating chip, and on filling, a shine sweeps the track, the bar drains, the readout carries the level up, a badge flips, and sparks ring out. Taps during the ceremony queue rather than drop — a progress toy that loses your taps is a bug wearing a costume.

props.name: perClick / levelUpAt
props.description: XP per tap, and the threshold.

props.name: startLevel
props.description: Where the readout begins.

props.name: onLevelUp
props.description: Fires with the new level.

usageNotes: The level numeral is the house readout, so the carry from 9 to 10 rolls exactly like every other number in the system.
Taps during the level-up sequence accumulate and apply after — never dropped.
Reduced motion swaps bar, level, and badge instantly and keeps the caption flash.

items.title: Streak Flame
items.tagline: It grows. It flares. It goes out.
items.description: A streak counter whose flame grows with the number: body and core flicker on the same period but different phases, so the two never sync and the whole thing reads alive. Extending it surges the flame and lifts embers; milestones flare. Break the streak and it gutters out to a wisp of smoke, which is exactly as unpleasant as it should be.

props.name: streak
props.description: The starting count.

props.name: onMilestone
props.description: Fires at 7, 30, and every 30 after.

usageNotes: Flame size steps through fixed brackets, so the growth is legible rather than continuous creep.
The desynced core is the whole illusion — same duration, offset delay; do not sync them.
Reduced motion holds a still flame at its bracket and shows milestone rings as a state.

items.title: Glint Trophy
items.tagline: The shelf remembers your favourites.
items.description: A shelf of four trophies that slide up on arrival and then take turns catching the light — one glint at a time, on a calm cycle, never two at once. Polish one and it wiggles, sparkles, and stays permanently a little brighter, so the shelf quietly records what you have fussed over. Dusting resets the whole thing.

props.name: onPolish
props.description: Fires with the polished trophy's name.

usageNotes: One shared glint slot makes overlapping sweeps structurally impossible, not merely unlikely.
Brightness caps after three polishes so the shelf cannot be bleached white.
Reduced motion presents the shelf filled, flashes a static highlight on click, and still brightens.

items.title: Fortune Crack
items.tagline: Snap it. Read it. Get back to work.
items.description: A fortune cookie that squeezes, snaps into two settled halves, drops three crumbs, and unfurls a paper slip with a dry line printed on it. Click again and it re-fuses with the next fortune queued. The fortunes are workplace-plain rather than mystical, which makes them land.

props.name: fortunes
props.description: Override the built-in six; they cycle in order.

props.name: onCrack
props.description: Fires with the revealed line.

usageNotes: Fortunes cycle from a counter, never at random — a demo replays identically for everyone.
The slip unfurls by scaling its height from a sliver, which reads as paper rather than a fade-in.
Reduced motion swaps straight to the cracked still with the slip and its text shown.

items.title: Spark Jar
items.tagline: Catch ten, then let them go.
items.description: Fireflies drifting across a dark card and a jar to catch them in: click one and it breaks from its drift, flies to the jar mouth, and settles inside bobbing while the glass glows one step warmer. Fill it and the lid taps shut, the jar blooms, and a moment later everything streams back out — the toy is a loop, not a wall.

props.name: capacity
props.description: Sparks before the jar is full (4–16).

props.name: onFull
props.description: Fires once when the jar fills.

usageNotes: The drifting field is a fixed five — capacity changes the counter, never the hook count.
Simultaneous landings are guarded against overshooting capacity or double-firing the callback.
Reduced motion parks the sparks, pockets catches instantly, and shows the full-jar bloom as a state.

items.title: Grow Sprout
items.tagline: Water it four times. Then again.
items.description: A seed you water into a flower, one click at a time: droplets fall, a stem draws upward, leaves unfurl, and a bud swells and blooms six petals in a cascade. A fifth click drops a seed back into the soil and the plant fades, leaving the cycle ready to run again. Growth staged as clicks rather than time, so nobody has to wait to see the bloom.

props.name: onBloom
props.description: Fires when the flower opens.

usageNotes: The stem draws with pathLength; petals rotate on plain wrappers and only scale on the motion child, sidestepping SVG origin trouble.
Every stage is click-driven and reversible by completing the cycle — nothing here is on a timer you must outwait.
Reduced motion swaps directly between fully-formed stage stills.

items.title: Dodge Button
items.tagline: Two dodges, then it gives up.
items.description: A button that plays hard to get exactly twice, then relents — approach it with a pointer and it springs to the next seat in a fixed cycle, and after two dodges it returns to centre and lets you click it. Keyboard users are never dodged, and neither are touch devices, because a button that runs away from a thumb is not a joke, it is a bug.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button claims it will do.

props.name: dodges
props.description: Evasions before it relents (0–4).

usageNotes: Keyboard focus and Enter or Space never trigger a dodge — the bit is pointer-only, by design.
Coarse pointers are exempt entirely; the button simply works on touch.
Reduced motion skips the bit and presents a normal button from the start.

items.title: Oracle Orb
items.tagline: Ask again Monday.
items.description: A fortune-telling orb with the mysticism removed: shake it and the fluid clouds, the die surfaces, and an answer fades in that sounds like it came from a colleague rather than a spirit. Answers cycle in fixed order, so a demo tells everyone the same fortunes in the same sequence — which is the only honest way to run an oracle.

props.name: answers
props.description: Override the built-in eight; they cycle in order.

props.name: onAnswer
props.description: Fires with each surfaced answer.

usageNotes: Re-shaking mid-answer restarts the sequence rather than queueing — that is how the real object behaves.
The mist is layered translucent gradients, not a blur filter, so it stays cheap.
Reduced motion swaps straight to the next answer with the die at rest.

items.title: Mood Gem
items.tagline: It can tell how you are moving.
items.description: A faceted gem that reads the room from how you move: quick passes make it restless, slow ones calm it, sitting still turns it content, and leaving makes it still. It rotates almost imperceptibly so the facets keep catching differently, and clicking sets the current mood for a few seconds regardless of what your hands do next.

props.name: onMood
props.description: Fires when the mood changes.

usageNotes: Mood is bucketed from speed and dwell, and state only changes when the bucket does — never per pointer move.
The idle rotation is deliberately too slow to notice directly; you only see that the light has changed.
Reduced motion drops the rotation and pulse, keeping instant colour changes and the caption.

items.title: Disco Floor
items.tagline: It dances when you look away.
items.description: A small dance floor that lights under your cursor with a soft falloff and, left alone for a moment, starts dancing on its own through authored patterns — sweeps, checkers, a pulse from the centre. Move back in and it yields to you immediately. Clicking drops a beat: everything flashes, then falls back in a cascade.

props.name: onBeat
props.description: Fires on the beat drop.

usageNotes: This is a lighting toy on a fixed grid, not a layout — reach for the tile grid when you need to arrange content.
Idle frames are an authored table, so the floor performs the same routine everywhere.
Reduced motion leaves the floor dark until hovered and drops the idle routine entirely.

items.title: Drum Pads
items.tagline: Visual instruments. Loud anyway.
items.description: Four squashy pads that hit like the real thing: each squashes under the strike and throws a burst matched to its voice — a thick ring for the kick, sharp lines for the snare, a fine spray for the hat, staggered arcs for the clap. Hit one repeatedly and the bursts grow. A strip beneath keeps the last eight hits, so you can see the groove you just played.

props.name: onHit
props.description: Fires with the struck pad's name.

usageNotes: A, S, D, F play the pads when the group has focus, so a rhythm can be played with both hands.
Repeat hits build a streak that grows the burst, decaying after a short pause — velocity you can see.
Reduced motion flashes the pad and still records the mark, with no squash or burst.

items.title: Snow Shake
items.tagline: Shake it. Then watch it settle.
items.description: A snow globe you shake by click or by drag, where the settling is the point: flakes lift off the drift, swirl on seeded paths, and come down staggered until the last one lands and the caption says so. Every flake's path is derived from its index, so the same shake happens for everyone — a snow globe with no randomness in it at all.

props.name: flakes
props.description: Flakes in the dome (6–24).

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires when the last flake lands.

usageNotes: Drag energy scales the rock and the swirl duration — a hard shake really does snow longer.
Flake paths come from seeded per-index constants, never a random source.
Reduced motion redistributes the flakes and settles them in two instant steps.

items.title: Zen Rake
items.tagline: Three grooves that heal themselves.
items.description: A sand garden and a three-tooth comb: drag and three parallel grooves follow your hand, offset along the path normal so the rake reads as a rake. Strokes rest for a few seconds and then heal, the bed holding only its last six so it never silts up. Arrow keys rake too, for anyone gardening from the keyboard.

props.name: onStroke
props.description: Fires per completed stroke.

usageNotes: Points are only recorded every few pixels, so a long drag stays cheap and the curve stays smooth.
Strokes cap at six and heal on a timer — the bed is self-cleaning by design.
Reduced motion draws grooves at full opacity and removes them outright instead of fading.

items.title: Wind Chimes
items.tagline: Still, breath, gust, squall.
items.description: Five graduated tubes that sway from the breeze your cursor makes, each on its own natural period so they never move in unison — that desync is the entire effect. Contacts with the clapper flash in sequence rather than at once, and a click plays a full run down the scale. The caption names the weather you are making.

props.name: onRing
props.description: Fires on a full run.

usageNotes: Breeze is bucketed into four states; only a bucket change restarts the sways, never a pointer move.
Contacts come from fixed per-tube phases rather than collision maths — cheaper, and it reads better.
Reduced motion hangs the tubes still, keeps the weather caption, and brightens them in sequence on click.

items.title: Ferris Glow
items.tagline: The cabins stay level. That is the trick.
items.description: A little ferris wheel turning at dusk, with the detail that matters: the cabins counter-rotate so they stay level however far the wheel has come around. Cabin and rim lights pulse on offset phases so the whole thing twinkles instead of blinking, hovering speeds the turn, and a click lights every bulb at once before they settle back in a cascade.

props.name: cabins
props.description: Cabins on the rim (6–12).

props.name: onLight
props.description: Fires when every bulb lights.

usageNotes: One shared transform counter-rotates every cabin — one hook, reused, regardless of cabin count.
Rim positions are index maths, so the wheel is identical on server and client.
Reduced motion parks the wheel at a pleasing angle with lights at mid brightness.

items.title: Sky Bloom
items.tagline: Tap the sky. Mind the gravity.
items.description: Fireworks you set off yourself: click anywhere in the night sky and a rocket rises from the skyline beneath your finger, decelerating to apex before blooming into twelve sparks that arc and droop under authored gravity. Three may be in the air at once, palettes cycle so consecutive shots differ, and the sky brightens a touch with each one.

props.name: onBloom
props.description: Fires per firework with the running total.

usageNotes: The rocket launches from the skyline at your click's x — the shot always comes from the ground, not the cursor.
Three concurrent fireworks is the cap; further clicks wait rather than piling up.
Reduced motion paints the bloom at the click point with its sparks already landed, then fades it.

items.title: Mail Fold
items.tagline: It folds, it seals, it goes.
items.description: A letter that folds itself into an envelope and leaves: the bottom third comes up, the top third comes down, a flap sweeps over, a seal presses on, and the whole thing tilts off the top-right corner trailing a dash of its own path. A fresh sheet drops in behind it. For sent-confirmations that deserve more than a checkmark.

props.name: onSent
props.description: Fires as the envelope leaves.

usageNotes: Folds scale from their own hinge edges — plain HTML transform origins, no 3D and no Safari surprises.
Clicks during the sequence are ignored; the letter always finishes leaving.
Reduced motion steps three stills: flat, sealed, gone.

items.title: Fridge Poetry
items.tagline: Ten words. No wrong answers.
items.description: Word magnets on a fridge door, draggable into whatever sentence you like — each lands on a loose grid with a small jiggle that sells the weight of the magnet, and the one you touched last sits on top. Arrow keys move them a cell at a time, because a drag-only toy quietly excludes half its audience.

props.name: words
props.description: Override the built-in ten.

props.name: onArrange
props.description: Fires with each moved word.

usageNotes: Positions live in one state array; only the dragged magnet rides motion values, so hook count never varies.
Landing snaps to a 12px grid — loose enough to feel hand-placed, tight enough to line up.
Reduced motion keeps 1:1 dragging with instant snaps and no jiggle.

items.title: Juggle Loop
items.tagline: Three, then four, then dropped.
items.description: Three balls in a proper cascade, each on the same authored arc offset by a third of the cycle, with hands that dip as they catch. Click to add a ball up to five — the tempo tightens to keep it plausible — and one more click drops the lot before starting over. Hovering runs it in slow motion, which is when you can see the pattern.

props.name: balls
props.description: Starting count (3–5).

props.name: onDrop
props.description: Fires when the pattern collapses.

usageNotes: Every ball runs the same keyframe arc with a phase delay — no per-ball hooks, so the count is free to change.
Hover scales the durations rather than restarting the loop, so slow motion never resets the pattern.
Reduced motion arranges the balls in a still tableau and keeps the counting.

items.title: Rocket Drill
items.tagline: Three, two, one, and back again.
items.description: A launch with a countdown and, unusually, a recovery: three numerals pop while the rocket trembles harder, the gantry swings clear, it climbs out of frame on smoke, and then a parachute drifts the capsule back down to the pad. Most launch animations forget the coming-back part, which is the half that makes it a drill.

props.name: onLaunch / onRecover
props.description: Fires at liftoff, and again on landing.

usageNotes: The tremble escalates per count — the suspense is built from the same jitter at three amplitudes.
Every chained beat is a tracked timer, so an unmount mid-drill leaves nothing running.
Reduced motion steps the stills: pad, countdown, empty sky, parachute, landed.

items.title: Claw Drop
items.tagline: It always catches. That is the joke.
items.description: A claw machine that always catches — the honesty is the joke. The trolley sweeps the rail so you still have to time it, but wherever you stop, the claw takes the nearest plush, lifts it, and delivers it down the chute to the tray. Clear the bed and it restocks. No odds, no coins, no disappointment.

props.name: onCatch
props.description: Fires with the caught plush's index.

usageNotes: The catch is a nearest-index lookup against the frozen trolley position — deterministic, and the machine never cheats.
The bed empties as you win and restocks in a cascade once cleared.
Reduced motion parks the trolley and cycles through the remaining plushes so the toy still progresses.

items.title: Quest Log
items.tagline: Finishing one opens the next.
items.description: A quest list built to be finished: each advance rolls its counter and fills its bar, and completing one sweeps the row, flies its reward to the running total, and unlocks the next quest in the chain. The unlock is the hook — a log that opens its own next line is harder to close than one that simply ends.

props.name: quests
props.description: The log; each carries a target and an XP reward. Defaults to five work-flavoured quests.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires as a quest closes.

usageNotes: Rewards fly to the header total, which carries on the house readout — the same roll every number in the system uses.
Locked rows are genuinely inert; the chain only opens as its predecessor closes.
Reduced motion drops the sweeps and flights but keeps every state legible.

items.title: Skill Tree
items.tagline: Spend a point, open two doors.
items.description: A talent tree you spend points into: available nodes pulse for attention, spending one fills the node, draws the link from its parent, and cascades any newly-eligible node into reach. The capstone sweeps the whole tree. Respec drains it all back in reverse, because a build you cannot undo is a build nobody experiments with.

props.name: points
props.description: Points available to spend.

props.name: onUnlock
props.description: Fires per node owned.

usageNotes: The layout is an authored table in a fixed viewBox — nothing is measured, so the tree is identical on server and client.
Links draw with pathLength as the tree grows and undraw on respec.
Reduced motion swaps node states and shows links complete, with no pulses or draws.

items.title: Rank Insignia
items.tagline: Five tiers, and a real ceiling.
items.description: A rank badge that promotes with the ceremony a promotion deserves: the old insignia clears in a flash, the new one lands on a spring, a chevron stamps on, light sweeps the plate, and the name rolls over. Five tiers, and an honest ceiling at the top instead of invented infinite ranks.

props.name: tier
props.description: Starting tier, 0 to 4.

props.name: onPromote
props.description: Fires with the new tier and its name.

usageNotes: Chevron count equals the tier, so the rank is readable without the label.
The top tier fills a bar that never completes and says so — no fake progression.
Reduced motion swaps the insignia and keeps the caption flash.

items.title: Combo Meter
items.tagline: The bar is always draining.
items.description: A combo counter that drains while you watch, so every hit is relief as much as reward: landing one refills the bar, pops the numeral, and steps the multiplier at fixed thresholds — which shortens the fuse. Let it empty and the combo shatters, the panel cools, and your best score stays on screen as the reason to go again.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: Combo counts at which the multiplier steps up.

props.name: onBreak
props.description: Fires with the combo that was lost.

usageNotes: Higher multipliers drain faster — the reward and the pressure are the same dial.
The best-combo line is the retention device; do not remove it to save space.
Reduced motion steps the bar in visible increments instead of draining continuously.

items.title: Daily Check
items.tagline: The reason to open it tomorrow.
items.description: The seven-day check-in strip, built as a chain: claiming a day fills it, stamps it, flies its reward to the total, draws a connector to tomorrow, and hands the pulse to the next tile. Day seven pays out and the week rolls over with the streak intact. It never reads the clock — days are indexes, so the strip renders identically on the server and every visit.

props.name: rewards
props.description: Per-day rewards; the length drives the strip (5–7).

props.name: startDay
props.description: Which day reads as today, so history is visible.

props.name: onClaim
props.description: Fires per claim.

usageNotes: No clock is read anywhere — days are indexes, which keeps SSR deterministic and demos reproducible.
Breaking the streak is a visible, legible loss; that is what makes the chain worth keeping.
Reduced motion claims instantly and keeps the totals and captions.

items.title: Loot Chest
items.tagline: The shudder before the lid.
items.description: A chest that spends longer on the anticipation than the payoff: it shudders three times with rising amplitude, the clasp pops, light leaks from the seam, and only then does the lid swing and the beam erupt. The card that rises carries a rarity, and the reaction scales with it — legendary earns the sweep, common earns a settle and nothing more.

props.name: rarities
props.description: The tier table — name, tint, pip count. Cycled in fixed order, never rolled.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires with the revealed tier.

usageNotes: Rarity is a fixed cycle, not a random roll — a demo that rolls differently for every visitor cannot be reasoned about.
Reaction intensity is tiered on purpose; celebrating every outcome equally teaches nothing.
Reduced motion opens straight to the card with its rarity styling intact.

items.title: Prize Wheel
items.tagline: The deceleration is the ride.
items.description: A segmented wheel whose last half-second is the whole experience: a wind-up counter-rotation, several turns, then a hard deceleration onto the segment with the pointer ticking slower as it goes. The blank segment lands flat on purpose — muted caption, no sparks — because a wheel that celebrates nothing is a wheel nobody reads.

props.name: segments
props.description: The wedges; wedge angles derive from the count. Outcomes cycle in fixed order.

props.name: onLand
props.description: Fires with the winning label.

usageNotes: Outcomes are a fixed cycle — the wheel never rolls, so demos and tests are reproducible.
The distinct cousin in Selection is wheel-picker, a scrolling input; this is a reward device.
Reduced motion jumps to the result angle and highlights the winner without spinning.

items.title: Pack Tear
items.tagline: Tear it. Fan it. Flip it.
items.description: A foil pack you actually tear: the rip tracks your drag one-to-one, shedding flecks, and commits past two thirds. Five cards fan out face-down, and each flip is its own verdict with rarity-scaled reaction. The haul line totals what you pulled, then a fresh pack reseals with the next set queued.

props.name: cards
props.description: Cards in the pack (3–7).

props.name: onReveal
props.description: Fires per card flipped.

usageNotes: Flips scale to zero and back rather than rotating in 3D — Safari-proof, no perspective needed.
Enter, Space, or arrow keys tear in steps; the ritual is never drag-only.
Rarities cycle in fixed order, so a pack opens the same way for everyone.

items.title: Gacha Capsule
items.tagline: Crank, drop, crack, collect.
items.description: A capsule machine with the full ritual: crank it round, watch the capsule bounce down the chute, wobble to rest, crack along its seam, and present what is inside. Tiers cycle in fixed order and the top one is deliberately infrequent — a machine that hands out rainbows every turn is not a machine anyone remembers.

props.name: onPrize
props.description: Fires with the revealed tier.

usageNotes: The crank is 1:1 direct manipulation with unwrapped angle accumulation; a full turn dispenses.
The rare tier is rationed by the cycle, not by odds — honest pacing beats fake probability.
Reduced motion presents the opened capsule and updates the shelf instantly.

items.title: Reward Track
items.tagline: The unclaimed count is the mechanic.
items.description: The season track, built around its real mechanic: the unclaimed counter. Progress advances a head along the ribbon, nodes it passes start pulsing, and the nag ticks up until you claim them. Milestones every fifth node pay bigger, and finishing the track offers the next season rather than pretending the run goes on forever.

props.name: nodes
props.description: The ribbon of rewards; every fifth reads as a milestone.

props.name: perClick
props.description: Progress per earn, with nodes spaced 100 apart.

props.name: onClaim
props.description: Fires per claimed node.

usageNotes: The track scrolls inside its own container at narrow widths — the page never scrolls sideways.
Claim-all runs a cascade so a backlog clears as one satisfying sweep.
Reduced motion jumps the head and claims instantly, keeping every count legible.

items.title: Leaderboard Climb
items.tagline: The row above yours has a name.
items.description: A leaderboard whose whole point is the row with your name on it: score a round and the list resorts, your row physically travelling past the ones it overtook and nudging each on the way. The rival directly above you is named and marked, because a target you can read is worth more than a rank you cannot.

props.name: players
props.description: The board; exactly one entry carries the `you` flag.

props.name: gains
props.description: The fixed cycle of per-round scores. Never random.

usageNotes: Reordering rides motion layout, so rows travel rather than teleport — the travel is the component.
The gap line and the next-rival mark are the retention devices; keep them.
Reduced motion reorders instantly and drops the nudges and flights.

items.title: Versus Bar
items.tagline: The lead keeps changing hands.
items.description: A tug-of-war between two sides on a single bar: each push moves the seam, consecutive pushes build a surge that pushes further, and a push the other way resets it — which is where the drama lives. Crossing the centre names the new leader, and past eighty percent the losing side starts showing the brink.

props.name: left / right
props.description: The two sides, each with a name and tint.

props.name: step
props.description: Percent the seam moves per push, before surge.

usageNotes: Surge multiplies the step by streak length from a fixed table — momentum is legible, not simulated.
The brink marker past eighty percent is what makes a comeback readable.
Reduced motion jumps the seam and keeps every caption.

items.title: Bracket Run
items.tagline: Eight enter. The table decides.
items.description: An eight-entrant elimination bracket that plays out one match at a time: both slots tense, the loser dims and strikes through, and the winner's name travels the connector into the next round as the line draws in behind it. Outcomes come from a fixed table — a bracket that reseeds itself every visit cannot be reasoned about.

props.name: entrants
props.description: Eight names; short lists pad from the defaults.

props.name: onChampion
props.description: Fires when the final resolves.

usageNotes: The layout and every outcome are authored constants — nothing is measured and nothing is rolled.
Eliminations are as legible as advances; the strike-through is not decoration.
The bracket scrolls inside its own container at narrow widths.

items.title: Score Tick
items.tagline: A thousand should hit harder than fifty.
items.description: An arcade scoreboard with tiered juice: bigger points pop harder, throw more flecks, and float a larger chip, so a thousand lands differently from fifty. Consecutive presses build a chain that decays on its own. Passing the high score is the beat the whole component is built around, and it gets the room it deserves.

props.name: values
props.description: The three award buttons.

props.name: startHigh
props.description: The score to beat.

usageNotes: Numerals are the house readout — the carry from 999 to 1000 is the same roll as everywhere else in the system.
Reset zeroes the score but keeps the best; the standing record is the reason to play again.
Reduced motion keeps the rolls and captions, drops the pops and flecks.

items.title: Podium Rise
items.tagline: Third, second, first. Always that order.
items.description: A results podium that reveals in reverse — third, second, first — because saving the winner is the entire dramaturgy. Plinths rise, cards land, scores roll up from zero, and first place takes an overshoot, a crown, and a sweep. Clicking mid-ceremony skips to the finish: a results screen that traps you is a bad results screen.

props.name: places
props.description: First, second, third — in that order.

props.name: onReveal
props.description: Fires when the ceremony starts.

usageNotes: The pause before first place is longer than the others on purpose; that gap is the anticipation.
The ceremony is skippable and the skip clears every pending timer.
Reduced motion shows all three places at once in their final state.

items.title: Timing Bar
items.tagline: Stop it in the narrow band.
items.description: The bar every crafting game teaches you to hit: a marker sweeps, you stop it, and the hit-test reads the marker's live motion value rather than any state — which is what makes the judgement honest. The perfect zone sits deliberately off-centre so it has to be learned, and every success speeds the next sweep while narrowing the target.

props.name: onResult
props.description: Fires per attempt with the judgement.

usageNotes: The judgement reads the live motion value in the handler — never state, which would lag a frame and lie.
A miss resets both the streak and the difficulty; the loss has to be legible or the streak means nothing.
Reduced motion steps the marker in discrete positions so the skill check survives without continuous motion.

items.title: Rhythm Tap
items.tagline: Sixteen steps, and your timing.
items.description: A single lane, an authored sixteen-step pattern, and a hit zone: notes arrive on the beat and you tap them, judged perfect, good, or missed against a step clock rather than any DOM position. Combo, best, and a rolling accuracy figure sit above it. It starts paused, so nothing moves until someone asks it to.

props.name: pattern
props.description: Which steps carry a note; a fixed authored table by default.

props.name: tempo
props.description: Milliseconds per step.

usageNotes: Judgement is step arithmetic off an interval counter — no wall clock, no DOM measurement.
It starts paused by design; an autoplaying rhythm lane in a docs page is a nuisance.
Reduced motion pulses the hit zone on the beat instead of travelling notes.

items.title: Accuracy Ring
items.tagline: It tells you how wrong you were.
items.description: A ring shrinking toward a target you tap when they match — and then it tells you the signed error in pixels, so you learn whether you are early or late. That readout is the whole teaching device. Success speeds the next ring and narrows the band; a miss resets both.

props.name: onResult
props.description: Fires with the judgement and the signed error.

usageNotes: The signed error is the point — a bare hit or miss teaches nothing about which way to adjust.
The hit-test reads the ring's live motion value, never state.
Reduced motion steps the ring through fixed radii so the check still exists.

items.title: Power Gauge
items.tagline: Max power is the trap.
items.description: Hold to charge, release to commit — and the needle does not stop at full, it oscillates, so overcharging is a real risk and waiting for the second pass is a real strategy. The sweet spot sits below maximum on purpose: max power is a trap, and the overcharge result is visibly worse than a good one.

props.name: onShot
props.description: Fires on release with the band and the value.

usageNotes: The release reads the needle's live motion value; a release always lands even if the pointer left the button.
The best marker stays pinned on the result bar — chasing your own best is the loop.
Reduced motion steps the needle on an interval while held, judging identically.

items.title: Reflex Light
